newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Politics hit Paris stocks, Frankfurt down.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Politics hit Paris stocks, Frankfurt down.

text.p: A sudden bout of political jitters drove French stocks down sharply on Friday and German shares were badly hit by a weaker dollar and a poor overnight showing on Wall Street.
The Paris bourse dropped 2.25 percent on worries over a snap election. Frankfurt lost over one percent as the falling dollar dimmed export prospects but London was flat.

The U.S. currency slipped against the mark after the German central bank chief President Hans Tietmeyer's comments on Thursday that the Bundesbank was not interested in seeing the mark weaken further.

The big fall in the French CAC 40 index came after President Jacques Chirac failed to calm rumours on Thursday about a snap election or cabinet reshuffle, and the opposition Socialist party said it was ready to contest a vote.

The Socialists have accused Chirac of considering parliamentary elections a year early to renew the centre-right majority before a new bout of austerity to help France qualify for a single European currency.
"There is some selling. But absolutely no panic. People are just being cautious due to political uncertainties," one broker said.
The market was likely to remain volatile over the next few days as investors await to see if the French parliament is dissolved, brokers said.
Another broker said some investors were worried the dissolution of parliament might pave the way for a new austerity plan in France ahead of the euro single currency.
"There is some concern over a new austerity plan and its possible impact on economic growth," one broker said.
In Frankfurt, stocks were also well down, partially catching up with losses in after-hours electronic trade last night, and also because of the dollar and New York's negative close.
But trade was thin and dealers said the market lacked clear direction going into the weekend. "We haven't had any real orders," said a trader. "Things are just creaking along."

London, Europe's biggest bourse, was the best performer, slipping only a few points. But the market was lethargic as pre-election nerves and fears of rising interest rates put a lid on active trading.
"We've totally decoupled from the Dow," one trader said as the FTSE index was barely moved from Thursday's closing level of 4,298.9 points."We seem to be stuck around the 4,300 level."
The Dow broke its three-day winning streak on Thursday to finish 21.27 points or 0.32 percent lower at 6,658.60, after jumping 288 points in the previous three sessions.
Shares in British Telecommunications Plc firmed 7-1/2p to 450 at one point after news of a global alliance with its merger partner MCI Communications and Telefonica de Espana.
On currency markets, the dollar slipped against the mark and yen at the European midday, its energy sapped by dollar-dampening comments out of Japan and Germany.

Traders said an absence of economic data from the U.S. and Germany was making European trade lethargic, adding that the approach of the weekend and a G7 finance ministers' meeting next week was adding to the reluctance to stir up the market.
The dollar lost nearly a pfennig in early trade, because of Teitmeyer's remarks, before recovering slightly.
"The Germans have given up their long-standing silence on exchange rates...and that's made a pretty significant impact on the market," DMG's Baader said.

Against the yen, the dollar started the day weaker before perking up slightly. It had been hit by remarks made overnight by Eisuke Sakakibara, the influential head of the Japanese Finance Ministry's international finance bureau.

Sakakibara, in an interview with Reuters, warned of the danger of assuming Japan would not raise interest rates within the next year, saying it would be natural for the Bank of Japan to raise interest rates when the strength of the economy was confirmed.
CURRENCIES AT 1100 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7168 marks and 125.86 yen after ending at 1.7241 and 125.97 in late trading in Europe on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1100 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 2.8 points at 4,296.1.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 56.63 points at 2,558.87
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 31.86 points at 3,351.39.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in London at $342.00 versus $343.15 at the close in London on Thursday. Silver was three cents lower at $4.73.
